items.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019
items.q: And he booked Cannonball’s group and I was just a kid in high school and Cannonball’s piano player got busted for something. So he calls my mother, middle of the night, and says, “Mrs. Longo, you think you could let young Michael come down to finish the week with us?”

ctx.x: Oh see, back then, this was before rock & roll. And so, I don’t know if you remember Earl Bostic, you remember him? The kind of stuff he was playing is what was popular because Elvis and all that stuff hadn’t started yet. So we’d be playing “Night Train” and if you knew the blues, down there, in Florida, I don’t know man whether anybody — but the term “rhythm & blues” meant the changes to “I Got Rhythm” and blues changes. So when you played a rhythm & blues gig, if you could play “I Got Rhythm” changes and blues…

album. Because I played with him at this club called Porky’s in Fort Lauderdale. You know those Porky movies? That was a real place. That was Fort Lauderdale and in the movie it was Angel Beach. And they had Porky as this redneck guy with a cowboy hat. No, man, Porky was a gangster. He was Porky Pineko. And he loved jazz.
